social networks, education and self-perceived deprivation have the strongest effects on lottery play, while culture plays a much lesser explanatory role.
the poor play the lotteries because they are poor, not vice versa.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lottery play is not simply an individual choice but a collective action.
the poor play the lotto more because their friends play more and because they feel deprived.

the social structural factors that make it more difficult for the poor to achieve upward social mobility, and which make the poor more likely to be socially deprived, are the same factors that make the poor more vulnerable to lottery gambling.
